label: Nativist Party Does Not Run
detail: The nativist party's nominee never enters the race, leaving only the two main parties' tickets on the ballot.
assumption: Voters who backed the third candidate in 1856 are redistributed among the two major nominees or stay home, in line with how comparable voters behaved when the third candidate was absent.
facts_text: The nativist party that would lengthen naturalization and keep the foreign-born from office has decided to put forward no candidate for President.

Its former nominee, who had been put forward by it and who seeks to quiet the slavery question, announced earlier in the campaign that he would not stand, and its electors have been withdrawn from the ballots.
research_questions: Where third-party voters in 1856 had no candidate of their own, which major ticket did former Whigs and nativists choose, and how many abstained?
How did old-line Whig voters in the border and upper South behave when forced to choose between the two major parties?
Did nativist voters in the North lean toward the new anti-slavery-extension party or the administration party when the nativist ticket was absent?
source_text: Millard Fillmore and the American (Know-Nothing) Party don't run in 1856.
